helpful: The statpack interim section's per-Term substantive counts made the strictly-prior pooled baseline (30/225) a two-line computation.
Reading interim_signals.py clarified exactly which docket text resolves each ladder claim, which changed my amicus-increment number materially.
CourtListener docket-entries on the originating CA1 docket supplied the whole appellate posture (panel split, both stay denials) that the SCOTUS snapshot alone could not.
gaps: No conditional grant-rate cut by escalation signal (e.g. grant rate among response-requested substantive applications) exists anywhere; the signal counts published are right-censored and unconditioned, so the ladder can only be priced by judgment.
Interim cells get no record/documents/ text (application, response, amicus briefs), so the ask's strength and the response's arguments are invisible; even first-page text would help.

No sanctioned way to check for a companion SCOTUS application without risking outcome retrieval: a pipeline-provided related-application field (pre-cutoff, metadata only) would remove a real uncertainty in consolidated interim matters.
fedcourts corpus-info does not run against the service backend, so a cell cannot print the corpus vintage the freshness rule asks for; row-level last_live_polled stamps were the workaround.
notes: Recency-ranked query output is dominated by the current Term's applications (all denied so far), so the ranked prior pull added little beyond the statpack for this stage.
